# CSCI 435 PR review

You are drafting a code review that the user (GitHub login `ab-wm`) will test, edit and post on a
teammate's PR in `CSCI-435-SE/gitea`, a course fork of Gitea. The review is a graded course
deliverable, so the user stays its author: you gather the facts, check them, and hand back a
draft in their format. Don't post, approve or comment on the PR, and don't push to it. Don't offer
to fix the author's code either. In this course the author makes each change themselves, one
change per commit.

The user's standing instruction for reviews is "not *that* deep". That doesn't mean overlooking
real problems, and it doesn't mean nitpicking every small one. The code is not going upstream. A
finding belongs in the draft only if it would change a score, or if the author would want to know
about it before merging.

## 1. Find your footing

Work out where you are running, because that decides how you fetch the PR and where the draft goes.

- **Claude Code inside the repo clone** (`gh` works, and the working tree is the fork). Use `gh`
  for PR data and read source files locally. The user is usually on their own feature branch, so
  don't switch it. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr-<N>` and read files
  with `git show pr-<N>:<path>`. Compare with `git diff origin/main...pr-<N>`, because local
  `main` is often behind.
- **Chat, or anywhere without the clone.** The repo is public. Use a GitHub connector if one is
  attached. Otherwise fetch the URLs in `references/fetching-without-the-repo.md`. If nothing can
  reach GitHub, ask the user for the PR link and the diff.

## 2. Triage

First get the PR's title, author, changed files and linked issue (`Closes #N`). Then decide how
much review it needs. The user only does a full review when code changed:

- **The PR is already merged, or the user has already reviewed it.** Say so first, quoting their
  existing review in a line. Continue only if they want a fresh look, for example a re-review
  after new commits. Don't let their earlier scores steer yours.
- **The PR only touches check-ins, docs, course files, showcase material, AI logs, or config like
  `.coderabbit.yaml`.** Skip the rubric. Skim the files for anything surprising, such as code
  hiding in a "docs" PR, a secret, or a file in the wrong folder. Then suggest a one-line
  approval in the user's voice, for example "All good, just the check-in doc and AI log. No need
  for complete review."
- **The PR is the user's own.** Nobody approves their own PR in this course. Say so, and offer a
  list of findings instead of a rubric.
- **This is a follow-up after the user asked for changes.** Check only the items they asked for.
  If those are done, suggest a short approval such as "All good now!"
- **The PR changes code or tests.** Do the full review described below.

## 3. Gather, lightly

Read these in order, and stop once you can score every rubric row:

1. The PR description, and the linked issue's acceptance criteria (ACs) and design decisions.
   The rubric is scored against the ACs.
2. The diff. Skip `ai-logs/**`: those files are thousands of lines of chat transcript, and they
   are not reviewed.
3. CodeRabbit's comments and the author's replies, so you don't repeat what was already raised
   and fixed.
4. The CI status, if you can see it.
5. Just enough of the code the diff touches or depends on to check its claims. In the clone,
   `.claude-students/INDEX.md` lists short docs for each area if you need background.

Don't run lint, builds, servers or e2e suites unless the user asks. CI already runs lint and the
tests, and the user does their own hands-on testing. Don't split the review across subagents.

Aim for about 10–15 tool calls on a typical PR. In testing, runs that went to 35 calls produced
no better drafts than shorter ones would have. Spend those calls on checking the findings that
will go in the draft, one check each. Don't chase ideas you won't include. Don't read the
author's AI logs, and only download a library's source when a finding depends on it. If you go
over the budget, write the draft with what you have, and say what you didn't check.

## 4. What to check

- **Each AC.** Find where it is implemented and where it is tested. A missing AC is the main
  reason to lower the Correctness score.
- **Whether the tests can fail.** A test that would still pass with the feature removed doesn't
  count as coverage. Look for:
  - assertions that read a value without first asserting it exists;
  - `test.fail()` or skips that cover more than the one known failure;
  - checks that only test whether something is present.
- **Course rules that graders look at:**
  - a `## Tech Debt` section;
  - an AI assistance section;
  - before/after screenshots when templates, CSS or Vue files change;
  - Conventional Commit messages that end in `(#N)`;
  - `Assisted-by` trailers, and no `Co-Authored-By`;
  - commits small enough to review, for example split by layer.

  If you are unsure of the current sprint's rules, read `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, or
  fetch it.
- **Claims in the PR description.** Descriptions are often drafted by AI. Check one or two
  concrete claims against the code, such as a timing, a count, or "every test does X".

Check every finding against the source before it goes in the draft. Reviews of AI-written code
tend to produce confident findings that turn out wrong. A wrong finding in a posted review costs
the user more than a missed nit. If checking disproves your idea, drop the finding or reword it.
For example, on #105 a suspected "silent pass" turned out to fail loudly, so the finding became
about the unhelpful error message instead.

Leave out style nits, anything lint or CI catches, CodeRabbit findings the author already fixed
(credit those in one line), and anything that wouldn't change a score.

## 5. Scoring

Start every row at 10, and deduct points only for a concrete gap you can name. Past reviews show
how the user scores:

- A UI change without before/after screenshots: Documentation 8, Overall 9, "Yes, once the
  screenshots are added".
- One large commit instead of commits split by layer: AI transparency 7.
- A factual error in the description or the Tech Debt section: Documentation 8.
- Everything checks out: 10s, and Overall 10, "Yes".

A deduction needs a *required* point behind it, something you would ask the author to change before
merging. An observation you'd only file under "Strictly optional" (one AC covered by unit tests but not
end to end, a small AI-assisted commit the description doesn't mention) leaves the score at 10. The user
has scored a feature PR 10 on every row even though optional observations like these existed.

Overall is "Yes" unless something required is missing. Nits don't block a merge. Any score below
7 needs a note saying what would raise it, because the course rubric requires one.

## 6. Draft format

Use the rows from the course rubric. Read `.github/code-review-rubric.md` from the repo, or from
raw GitHub, so the draft picks up any change to the rubric. The template below matches the rubric
as of Sprint 2.

Write in the user's voice:

- short, plain sentences;
- one sentence per table note;
- no rule citations in the table;
- `file:line` for code findings.

Skim one of the reviews in `references/posted-examples.md` before you draft. These are reviews
the user actually posted.

```markdown
### Code Review — @ab-wm

TODO (you): what you ran, clicked or checked yourself.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |

### Strictly optional for completeness
**<the point in a few words>.** <one or two sentences, with file:line>

### AI-Log
Review was drafted by AI, and then changed to better fit the review structure and my inspection of the files. Log available on #<linked issue>.
```

- **Required changes** go in the note of the row they affect, written as a request ("please add
  before/after screenshots, as they are required"). Overall then says "Yes, once X is added".
- **Optional points** go in their own section after the table. Keep at most one or two, and drop
  the section if there are none.
- **The testing line** stays a visible `TODO`. It records what the user checked by hand, and they
  write it themselves. Don't fill it with what you did. A visible placeholder can't be posted by
  accident without being noticed.

## 7. Hand it back

- **In Claude Code**, write the draft to `.specstory/pr-<N>-review.md` (the folder is
  gitignored). If that file already exists, it may be the user's edited copy, so write the draft
  to `pr-<N>-review-2.md` (or the next free number) instead.
- **In chat**, give the draft as one fenced markdown block, so the table copies cleanly.

Then write a short summary in chat, about 10–15 lines:

- the verdict;
- each finding, marked required or optional;
- what you checked and what you didn't (for example, "didn't run the e2e suite"), so the user
  can write their testing line;
- any idea you couldn't verify, offered as something the user could try in their own testing.
  Unverified ideas never go in the draft.

End there. Remind the user to file this session's AI log as `ai-logs/README.md` describes, since
the AI-Log section points to it.

## What changed

Four Fomantic dropdown action menus on settings pages are now `<aria-menu>`:

- **Add Webhook**, in the shared `templates/repo/settings/webhook/base_list.tmpl`, so the repository, organisation, user and admin webhook pages all change at once (the admin page renders it twice).
- **The webhook type switcher** on the new and edit webhook forms (`templates/webhook/new.tmpl`). Its trigger is named "Webhook type: <type>" from the new key `repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher` (`"Webhook type: %s"`). The visible text and the label both come from one `$typeName` value, so they can't drift apart.
- **Link Account** on Settings → Security (`templates/user/settings/security/accountlinks.tmpl`).
- **Operations** above the System Notices table (`templates/admin/notice.tmpl`). The existing `.select.action` click handlers in `initAdminNotice` are unchanged, because `<aria-menu>` turns Enter and Space into `click()`.

So that the menus look the same as before (AC6), `web_src/css/modules/aria-menu.css` now copies what Fomantic gave them:

- Item text uses normal weight, so menus inside an `h4` header don't inherit its medium weight.
- `<img>` icons in items get Fomantic's spacing and vertical alignment. Most webhook icons and custom OAuth2 icons are `<img>`.
- A `.btn` trigger inherits its font weight (browsers reset it on buttons) and keeps the gap after a leading image.
- A neutral `.ui.button` trigger looks pressed while its menu is open, as `.ui.active.dropdown.button` did. This also brings back the pressed look on #108's Add File and folder menus.
- New `floating` host attribute for Fomantic's `ui floating dropdown` look: a 0.5em gap from the trigger and all corners rounded. It's documented in `aria.md` and in the `aria-menu.ts` header comment.

`web_src/css/modules/header.css` also drops the Fomantic margin from a button inside a header's `.ui.right` menu. Without that, the `bottom-end` menu would stick out 3px past the button.

## Why

Fomantic dropdowns keep focus on the wrapper and point at items with `aria-activedescendant`. With VoiceOver this breaks the arrow keys (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`). `<aria-menu>` moves real focus onto the items.

- **AC1:** Add Webhook is an `<aria-menu>` whose items are `link_menu.tmpl`'s links, with no `ui dropdown` class.
- **AC2:** the type switcher is an `<aria-menu>` named "Webhook type: Slack" (for example), not "Slack" alone.
- **AC3:** Link Account is an `<aria-menu>`, and each item links to `/user/oauth2/<name>`, path-escaped.
- **AC4:** Operations is an `<aria-menu placement="top-start">`. Select All, Deselect All and Inverse Selection work by keyboard and by mouse.
- **AC5:** Enter, Space and ArrowDown open each menu on its first item. Arrows, Home/End and type-ahead move focus. Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- **AC6:** position and look match in light and dark (screenshots below, with the small differences listed).
- **AC7:** the new Playwright tests cover adding a webhook and switching its type by keyboard, and the existing e2e and Go integration suites still pass.

## How it was tested

**Playwright: `tests/e2e/webhook-menus.test.ts` (new)**
- *Add webhook by keyboard*, from the repository settings page:
  - Enter opens on Gitea, End reaches Packagist, Escape returns focus.
  - Type-ahead `d` `d` moves Discord → DingTalk.
  - The menu's right edge lines up with the button (`bottom-end`).
  - Enter opens the DingTalk form. Pressing Enter in the URL field saves it, and the new webhook shows in the list.
- *Switch type by keyboard*:
  - The trigger and its menu are both named "Webhook type: DingTalk".
  - Enter, then `s`, focuses Slack, and Enter opens the Slack form.
  - The trigger is now named "Webhook type: Slack".

**Go integration**
- `TestNewWebHookLink` (updated): its old selector matches nothing after this change, and the test used to pass even when it found no items. It now checks that the list, new and edit pages contain `<aria-menu>` links and no Fomantic dropdown in the header (AC1/AC2).
- `TestUserSettingsSecurity/link_account_menu` (new): adds an OAuth2 source whose name contains spaces and checks for the escaped `/user/oauth2/test%20link%20source` item (AC3).
- `TestAdminNoticeOperationsMenu` (new): checks for the `top-start` menu with its three `.select.action` items (AC4).
- I checked that all three fail against the old templates and pass with the new ones.

**Not covered by e2e, checked by hand instead**
- AC3 and AC4 behaviour would need an OAuth2 login source and system notices. The e2e helpers can't create either, since notices only come from failed mirror or user-deletion jobs.
- So I checked them with a Playwright script against a local instance that has OAuth2 sources and notices:
  - Operations: Select All by Enter, Inverse Selection by Space and by type-ahead `i`, then Inverse and Deselect All by mouse. The checkboxes changed each time, and focus returned to Operations.
  - The org, user and admin webhook lists: 11 items each, no Fomantic dropdown left.
  - The edit-webhook switcher: named, and switching to Matrix by click works.
  - No JavaScript errors.
- For AC6, I compared screenshots and the computed boxes and fonts of each open menu, before and after.

The screenshots are cropped from 1280×720 captures, with each menu opened by mouse.

Add Webhook, the type switcher and Link Account are identical. Operations has three small differences:

- **Items are 14px instead of 13px.** Fomantic sized the items from the button's `small` class, because the button and the dropdown were one element. The items now use the standard menu size, as the commit Operations menu has since #108.
- **The button is 3px narrower.** `.ui.dropdown.button` reserved 22px of right padding for a caret this button never had.
- **The gap above the button is 7px instead of 5.5px**, because it is 0.5em of the larger font.

Placement: Fomantic picked a direction each time a menu opened, flipping it when it ran out of room. `<aria-menu>` uses a fixed placement, so each menu is set to where it opened at normal widths: `bottom-end` for the three right-aligned menus and `top-start` for Operations. One difference: Link Account used to flip upward when the button was near the bottom of the window, and now it always opens downward.

## Design

This follows the issue's Decision 1 (change only the two templates that include `link_menu.tmpl`) and Decision 2 (an `aria-label` built from the same `$typeName` as the visible text). Two things were added during implementation: the `floating` host attribute, and the CSS rules above that keep the old look.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- `<aria-menu>` has no automatic flip, so each placement is fixed in its template. A menu near the bottom of the window now opens off-screen and the page has to scroll, where Fomantic flipped it upward (seen with Link Account).
- The look-alike rules copy Fomantic's numbers (`0.78571429rem`, `0.5em`).
- The pressed-trigger rule lists the coloured button variants (`:not(.primary, .red, .green)`), so a new coloured variant used as a trigger needs adding there.
- `floating` is a new host attribute that only Operations uses so far. The pulse and dashboard `ui floating dropdown jump` menus can use it when they move over.

**Encountered:**
- `TestNewWebHookLink` passed even when its selector matched nothing. It now asserts the item count.
- Several Fomantic quirks behind the old look: `.ui.small.dropdown` resizing its items, 22px caret padding on a button with no caret, `.ui.dropdown > .ui.button { margin: 0 }`, and the `active` class on the open dropdown. Each is either copied or explained above.
- `./.claude-students/check.sh` already fails on `main` because `models-issues.md` is over its line cap. Left for a separate chore.

Move the "Add webhook", "Link account" and admin notice "Operations" menus to <aria-menu>
["Jack-Donohue"]
### User Story

As a keyboard or screen reader user configuring a repository, organisation, account or the site, I want the menus that add a webhook, link an external account or act on admin notices to be operable from the keyboard, so that settings pages don't block me in the places I configure integrations.

### User Scenario

An organisation owner using a screen reader opens **Settings → Webhooks**. They Tab to **Add webhook**, press Enter, type "d" twice to move from "Discord" to "DingTalk", and press Enter to open the new webhook form. On that form the type switcher at the top is read as "Webhook type: DingTalk, menu button", and they use it to switch to "Slack". A site admin opens **Site administration → System notices**, opens **Operations** above the table and picks "Select all".

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given the webhook list on the repository, organisation, user and admin settings pages (all rendered by `templates/repo/settings/webhook/base_list.tmpl`), when it renders, then **Add webhook** is an `<aria-menu>` whose items are the links from `templates/repo/settings/webhook/link_menu.tmpl`, and it has no `ui dropdown` class.
- [ ] AC2: Given the new webhook form (`templates/webhook/new.tmpl`), when it renders, then the type switcher is an `<aria-menu>`. Its trigger is named with both a localised "webhook type" label and the current type, not the type name alone.
- [ ] AC3: Given at least one OAuth2 sign-in source, when **Settings → Security** renders, then the **Link account** menu (`templates/user/settings/security/accountlinks.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>` and each provider item navigates to its `/user/oauth2/<name>` URL.
- [ ] AC4: Given **Site administration → System notices**, when it renders, then the **Operations** menu (`templates/admin/notice.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>` that opens upwards (`placement="top-start"`). "Select all", "Deselect all" and "Inverse selection" change the table checkboxes by keyboard and by mouse.
- [ ] AC5: Given each migrated menu, when operated by keyboard, then Enter/Space/ArrowDown opens it with focus on the first item, the arrows, Home/End and first-letter type-ahead move focus, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
- [ ] AC6: Given light and dark themes, when the migrated menus are compared before and after, then their position and look are the same, including the webhook icons. The PR includes before/after screenshots.
- [ ] AC7: Playwright tests cover adding a webhook from the repository settings page and switching the webhook type, both by keyboard. The existing e2e and Go integration suites still pass.

### Out of Scope

- Webhook form fields themselves (the content type and HTTP method `<select>`s and the events checkboxes).
- The admin list filter menus ("Sort", "Filter") in `templates/admin/*/list.tmpl`: they show a current selection, so they stay Fomantic like the other filters.
- Adding new webhook types or providers.

### Open Questions

- The AC2 label needs a new locale key, as no existing key says "webhook type". Is `repo.settings.webhook.type_switcher` an acceptable name? (A new key goes into `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` only.)
  - Yes: `"Webhook type: %s"`, filled from the same translated type name as the visible text.
- `link_menu.tmpl` lists 11 webhook types. Is type-ahead enough, or should the menu also get a maximum height and scroll?
  - Type-ahead only. The Fomantic menu had no maximum height either, and the 11 items fit on screen.

### Design Decision

### Decision 1: where to make the change
**Decision:** Change the two templates that wrap `link_menu.tmpl` (`base_list.tmpl` and `webhook/new.tmpl`), not each settings page. That one change covers the repository, organisation, user and admin webhook pages.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Change each settings page's template separately.
- (b) Leave the webhook menus on Fomantic and add only the missing names through the existing ARIA patch.

**Rationale:** All four pages already include `base_list.tmpl`, so (a) would copy the same markup four times and risk the copies drifting apart. (b) leaves the VoiceOver arrow key problem in `aria.md` unfixed. Upstream is also removing Fomantic (go-gitea/gitea#29849).

**Consequences:** Easier: one template change, one e2e test on the repository page, and the other three pages are covered by sharing the markup. Harder: `link_menu.tmpl` must keep its outer `.menu` element to be a valid `<aria-menu>` child, so it can't be reused as a plain list anywhere else without that wrapper.

### Decision 2: naming the type switcher
**Decision:** Give the new webhook form's type switcher an `aria-label` that combines a "webhook type" label with the current type.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Let the trigger take its name from its visible text, the current type alone.
- (b) Add a visible "Type:" text label next to the switcher.

**Rationale:** `aria.md` says a menu that only shows its current value needs a name of its own. "Slack, menu button" doesn't tell the user that the button switches the type. (b) also fixes that, but it changes the page's look, which AC6 rules out for this issue.

The switcher shows its current value, as the admin Sort and Filter menus do. But its items are links that open another type's form, not a choice kept on the page, so it is an action menu and moves to `<aria-menu>`. Sort and Filter stay on Fomantic (Out of Scope).

**Consequences:** Easier: the trigger is clear to screen readers and nothing changes visually. Harder: the label can fall out of sync with the visible text if someone later changes one and not the other, so the template should build both from the same `HookType` value.

### Scope

function initAdminNotice() {
  const pageContent = document.querySelector('.page-content.admin.notice');
  if (!pageContent) return;

  const detailModal = document.querySelector<HTMLDivElement>('#detail-modal')!;

  // Attach view detail modals
  queryElems(pageContent, '.view-detail', (el) => el.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const elNoticeDesc = el.closest('tr')!.querySelector('.notice-description')!;
    const elModalDesc = detailModal.querySelector('.content pre')!;
    elModalDesc.textContent = elNoticeDesc.textContent;
    showFomanticModal(detailModal);
  }));

  // Select actions
  const checkboxes = document.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>('.select.table .ui.checkbox input');

  queryElems(pageContent, '.select.action', (el) => el.addEventListener('click', () => {
    switch (el.getAttribute('data-action')) {
      case 'select-all':
        for (const checkbox of checkboxes) {
          checkbox.checked = true;
        }
        break;
      case 'deselect-all':
        for (const checkbox of checkboxes) {
          checkbox.checked = false;
        }
        break;
      case 'inverse':
        for (const checkbox of checkboxes) {
          checkbox.checked = !checkbox.checked;
        }
        break;
    }
  }));

## What changed

Two new anonymous-only feeds, plus a "Subscribe (iCal)" button on the Milestones, Issues and Pull
Requests lists:
- `/{owner}/{repo}/milestones.ics`
- `/{owner}/{repo}/issues.ics?state=open|closed|all`

What changed, by file:
- `services/feed/ical.go`: pure builder functions (`MilestonesICal`, `IssuesICal`, `ICalUID`) that
  turn rows into an RFC 5545 calendar with `github.com/arran4/golang-ical`. Every row becomes one
  all-day event, with:
  - a stable UID built from the database ID
  - the date taken in `DefaultUILocation`
  - CRLF line endings and 75-octet line folding
- `routers/web/feed/ical.go`: thin handlers. Each one:
  1. computes what an anonymous visitor may read
  2. returns 404 otherwise, even to signed-in members
  3. queries at most 1,000 rows
  4. writes the response as `text/calendar` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`
- `models/issues`: `Milestone.HasDeadline()` and a `FindMilestoneOptions.HasDeadline` filter (both
  treat `0` and the legacy year-9999 value as "no due date"), plus a `closestdeadline` issue sort
  ordered by `ABS(deadline_unix - now)`.
- `routers/web/web.go`: the two routes, behind the existing `feedEnabled` guard.
- List templates and handlers: the subscribe button. It renders only when the anonymous fetch would
  succeed.
- `go.mod` / `assets/go-licenses.json`: **new dependency** `github.com/arran4/golang-ical` v0.3.7
  (Apache-2.0, no transitive runtime dependencies).

## Why

Developers want repository deadlines next to their other events. This covers AC1-AC6:
- **AC1:** `milestones.ics` returns a VCALENDAR with `text/calendar; charset=utf-8`.
- **AC2:** `issues.ics` has one event per dated issue or PR, with the title, `#index` and URL.
- **AC3:** UIDs are stable across deadline changes, and `DTSTAMP` is the fetch time.
- **AC4:** a 1,000 cap that keeps the closest deadlines.
- **AC5:** 404 for private repositories and when feeds are disabled.
- **AC6:** the subscribe links.

## How it was tested / Test strategy

The format and date logic is pure and unit-tested without a database. Integration tests cover
routing and authorization.

- `services/feed/ical_test.go` (no DB) covers:
  - the UID surviving a deadline change
  - all-day dates in a UTC-5 zone, where a deadline at 23:59 local is the next day in UTC
  - title and URL formats for issues, PRs and milestones
  - undated rows being skipped
  - calendar properties
  - escaping of `, ; \` and newlines
  - CRLF endings and the 75-octet fold
  - a round-trip parse of the output
- `routers/web/feed/ical_test.go`: `?state=` parsing and the issue/PR unit filter.
- `models/issues`: `TestIssuesClosestDeadlineSort`, `TestMilestoneHasDeadline` and
  `TestFindMilestonesHasDeadline`.
- `tests/integration/repo_ical_test.go` covers:
  - both feeds on a public repo
  - the default state and `state=all`
  - the cap
  - a private repo returning 404 to anonymous users and to its owner
  - `ENABLE_FEED=false`
  - `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW=true` and `=expensive`
  - the button on Milestones, Issues and Pulls, and its absence on a private repo
  - a disabled pull-request unit dropping PRs from the feed
- `routers/common/blockexpensive_test.go`: documents that `issues.ics` is an "expensive" path.

## CI / manual verification

These passed locally on Windows (SQLite):
- `go test ./models/issues/ ./services/feed/ ./routers/web/feed/ ./routers/common/`
- `go test -tags 'sqlite sqlite_unlock_notify' -run '^(TestRepoICalFeeds|TestFeedRepo|TestFeedRepoContentTokenScopes)$' ./tests/integration/`
- `go mod tidy` (no changes beyond the new dependency) and `golangci-lint fmt`

Checked by hand: on a local instance I downloaded a public repo's `issues.ics` and opened it in
Outlook. The issues showed as all-day events on their deadline day, each titled with its
`owner/repo#index`.

Not run locally:
- `make lint-go`: golangci-lint's staticcheck analyzer crashes on the Go standard library with

- `.claude-students/check.sh`: it fails on line caps in `models-issues.md`, which this PR does not
  touch.

## Design

As in #100's Design Decision: `golang-ical`, handlers in `routers/web/feed/`, and UIDs from row IDs.
A code review during implementation added three refinements:
- the instance sign-in settings above are respected
- the calendar name uses the instance default language, because the response is publicly cacheable
- the milestone cap counts only dated milestones

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- A new direct dependency, `golang-ical`. The project is conservative about dependencies; the
  fallback is a small hand-written serializer.
- `Issues()` loads every attribute (labels, posters, ...), though the feed only needs titles.
- The legacy year-9999 "no due date" value is now a named constant in `models/issues/milestone.go`.
  `issue_search.go` still repeats the literal, and #98 has its own private copy. Unify them once
  both PRs are merged.

**Encountered:**
- `db.ListOptions.GetSkipTake` silently clamps page sizes to `MaxResponseItems` (50). `db.Find` and
  `Issues()` don't, which is why the 1,000 cap works. A future refactor to a helper that calls
  `GetSkipTake` would quietly cut the feed to 50.

Subscribe to a public repository's milestones and issue deadlines as an iCalendar feed
["vvchopra"]
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #36 

As a developer, I want to subscribe my calendar app to a public repository's milestone and issue
deadlines so that they appear next to my other events and update when the dates change in Gitea.


### User Scenario

Marco copies `https://gitea.example/octo/app/milestones.ics` and adds it in Google Calendar under
"From URL". Within the client's next refresh, "Sprint 3 (octo/app)" shows on the 14th as an
all-day event. A maintainer moves the milestone to the 21st. On the next refresh the existing
event moves to the 21st instead of a second event being added. He also subscribes to
`issues.ics?state=open` to see open issue deadlines.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a public repository, when an anonymous client GETs `/{owner}/{repo}/milestones.ics`,
  then the response is `200` with `Content-Type: text/calendar; charset=utf-8` and a valid
  VCALENDAR containing one all-day VEVENT per milestone with a due date.
- [ ] AC2: Given `/{owner}/{repo}/issues.ics`, when fetched, then it contains one all-day VEVENT
  per issue with a deadline (never one for `deadline_unix = 0`), with the issue title, `#index`,
  and a URL to the issue.
- [ ] AC3: Given a milestone or issue whose deadline changes, when the feed is fetched again, then
  the event keeps the same `UID` and has a newer `DTSTAMP`/`SEQUENCE`. A test checks that the UID
  of the same row is the same across two renders with different deadlines.
- [ ] AC4: Given a repository with more issues with deadlines than the cap (proposed 1,000), when
  `issues.ics` is fetched, then the response holds at most the cap, choosing the issues closest to
  today.
- [ ] AC5: Given a private repository, or feeds disabled with `[other] ENABLE_FEED = false`, when
  an anonymous client fetches either `.ics` URL, then it gets `404`, matching the RSS/Atom feeds.
- [ ] AC6: Given the repository's milestone and issue list pages, when viewed, then each shows a
  "Subscribe (iCal)" link to its feed.

### Out of Scope

- Private repositories and any token in the URL (issue C).
- The per-user cross-repository feed (issue D).
- Writing back to Gitea from the calendar (CalDAV).


### Open Questions

- Should the event `UID` use the instance's domain (`issue-{id}@{domain}`)? If so, changing
  `ROOT_URL` would duplicate events in clients that are already subscribed.
- Is 1,000 the right cap, and should it be a setting?

### Design Decision

**Decision:** Generate iCalendar with `github.com/arran4/golang-ical`. Serve it from new handlers
in `routers/web/feed/`, using the same `feedEnabled` guard and repo permission check the RSS/Atom
routes use. Build each UID from the row's database ID (`milestone-{id}@{domain}`,
`issue-{id}@{domain}`), never from the date.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Write the iCalendar text by hand.* RFC 5545 has strict rules for line folding, escaping and
  CRLF line endings that are easy to get wrong, and most calendar clients reject a malformed feed
  without any error message.
- *`github.com/emersion/go-ical`.* It covers RFC 5545 well and is maintained. But its API is
  lower-level, and it is aimed at CalDAV parsing rather than generating simple feeds.

**Rationale:** `golang-ical` is the common Go choice for generating feeds, and it handles folding
and escaping. Keeping the handlers in `routers/web/feed/` reuses the existing guard, permission
checks and route layout. IDs never change, so UIDs survive date edits and title renames.

**Consequences:** This adds a new dependency to `go.mod` (run `make tidy`). Because the project is
conservative about dependencies, raise it in the PR description, and upstream Gitea may push
back. The feed format is now a public contract: changing the UID scheme later would duplicate
every subscriber's events.


### Scope

diff --git a/routers/web/feed/ical.go b/routers/web/feed/ical.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..74c1a08cc2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/routers/web/feed/ical.go
@@ -0,0 +1,149 @@
+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package feed
+
+import (
+	"gitea.dev/models/db"
+	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
+	access_model "gitea.dev/models/perm/access"
+	"gitea.dev/models/unit"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/translation"
+	"gitea.dev/services/context"
+	feed_service "gitea.dev/services/feed"
+
+	ics "github.com/arran4/golang-ical"
+)
+
+// ICalMaxItems caps each calendar feed; a variable so tests can lower it
+var ICalMaxItems = 1000
+
+// anonymousRepoPermission is what calendar feeds serve: they never authenticate, so private repositories stay
+// hidden even from members until a dedicated calendar token exists
+func anonymousRepoPermission(ctx *context.Context, expensive bool) (access_model.Permission, error) {
+	if setting.Service.RequireSignInViewStrict {
+		return access_model.PermissionNoAccess(), nil // anonymous clients must sign in, which calendar apps cannot
+	}
+	if expensive && setting.Service.BlockAnonymousAccessExpensive { // blockexpensive.go matches the "/issues" prefix of issues.ics
+		return access_model.PermissionNoAccess(), nil
+	}
+	return access_model.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(ctx, ctx.Repo.Repository, nil)
+}
+
+// SetRepoICalFeedLink shows a list page's subscribe button only when an anonymous client could fetch the feed
+func SetRepoICalFeedLink(ctx *context.Context, feedName string, expensive bool) {
+	if !setting.Other.EnableFeed {
+		return
+	}
+	perm, err := anonymousRepoPermission(ctx, expensive)
+	if err != nil {
+		ctx.ServerError("anonymousRepoPermission", err)
+		return
+	}
+	if perm.CanReadAny(unit.TypeIssues, unit.TypePullRequests) {
+		ctx.Data["ICalFeedLink"] = ctx.Repo.RepoLink + "/" + feedName
+	}
+}
+
+// parseICalState maps ?state= to the IsClosed condition; anything unknown means open, the feed default
+func parseICalState(state string) optional.Option[bool] {
+	switch state {
+	case "closed":
+		return optional.Some(true)
+	case "all":
+		return optional.None[bool]()
+	default:
+		return optional.Some(false)
+	}
+}
+
+// icalIsPull limits the rows to the units an anonymous client can read; callers ensure at least one
+func icalIsPull(canReadIssues, canReadPulls bool) optional.Option[bool] {
+	switch {
+	case canReadIssues && canReadPulls:
+		return optional.None[bool]()
+	case canReadPulls:
+		return optional.Some(true)
+	default:
+		return optional.Some(false)
+	}
+}
+
+// readableICalPermission writes a 404 unless anonymous clients can read the repository's issues or pulls
+func readableICalPermission(ctx *context.Context, expensive bool) (access_model.Permission, bool) {
+	perm, err := anonymousRepoPermission(ctx, expensive)
+	if err != nil {
+		ctx.ServerError("anonymousRepoPermission", err)
+		return perm, false
+	}
+	if !perm.CanReadAny(unit.TypeIssues, unit.TypePullRequests) {
+		ctx.NotFound(nil)
+		return perm, false
+	}
+	return perm, true
+}
+
+func repoICalOptions(ctx *context.Context, nameKey string, now timeutil.TimeStamp) feed_service.ICalOptions {
+	repo := ctx.Repo.Repository
+	return feed_service.ICalOptions{
+		Name:         translation.NewLocale(setting.Langs[0]).TrString(nameKey, repo.FullName()), // public cache, so not the requester's language
+		RepoFullName: repo.FullName(),
+		RepoURL:      repo.HTMLURL(ctx),
+		Domain:       setting.Domain,
+		Location:     setting.DefaultUILocation,
+		Now:          now.AsTime(),
+	}
+}
+
+func writeICal(ctx *context.Context, cal *ics.Calendar) {
+	ctx.Resp.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/calendar; charset=utf-8")
+	ctx.Resp.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=300") // identical for every client, since it is anonymous-only
+	if err := cal.SerializeTo(ctx.Resp, ics.WithNewLineWindows); err != nil {
+		ctx.ServerError("Render iCalendar failed", err)
+	}
+}
+
+// RepoMilestonesICal serves the repository's milestone due dates as an iCalendar feed
+func RepoMilestonesICal(ctx *context.Context) {
+	if _, ok := readableICalPermission(ctx, false); !ok {
+		return
+	}
+	milestones, err := db.Find[issues_model.Milestone](ctx, issues_model.FindMilestoneOptions{
+		ListOptions: db.ListOptions{Page: 1, PageSize: ICalMaxItems},
+		RepoID:      ctx.Repo.Repository.ID,
+		IsClosed:    parseICalState(ctx.FormString("state")),
+		HasDeadline: true,
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		ctx.ServerError("FindMilestones", err)
+		return
+	}
+	now := timeutil.TimeStampNow()
+	writeICal(ctx, feed_service.MilestonesICal(repoICalOptions(ctx, "repo.ical.milestones_of", now), milestones))
+}
+
+// RepoIssuesICal serves the repository's issue and pull request deadlines as an iCalendar feed
+func RepoIssuesICal(ctx *context.Context) {
+	perm, ok := readableICalPermission(ctx, true)
+	if !ok {
+		return
+	}
+	now := timeutil.TimeStampNow()
+	issues, err := issues_model.Issues(ctx, &issues_model.IssuesOptions{
+		Paginator:             &db.ListOptions{Page: 1, PageSize: ICalMaxItems},
+		RepoIDs:               []int64{ctx.Repo.Repository.ID},
+		IsClosed:              parseICalState(ctx.FormString("state")),
+		IsPull:                icalIsPull(perm.CanRead(unit.TypeIssues), perm.CanRead(unit.TypePullRequests)),
+		HasDeadline:           optional.Some(true),
+		SortType:              "closestdeadline",
+		DeadlineReferenceUnix: int64(now),
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		ctx.ServerError("Issues", err)
+		return
+	}
+	writeICal(ctx, feed_service.IssuesICal(repoICalOptions(ctx, "repo.ical.issues_of", now), issues))
+}

diff --git a/services/feed/ical.go b/services/feed/ical.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..18b8355873
--- /dev/null
+++ b/services/feed/ical.go
@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package feed
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"time"
+
+	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
+	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
+
+	ics "github.com/arran4/golang-ical"
+)
+
+// ICalOptions carries everything a calendar needs besides its rows, so the builders stay free of request state
+type ICalOptions struct {
+	Name         string         // X-WR-CALNAME, what calendar apps call the subscription
+	RepoFullName string         // "owner/repo", shown in every event title
+	RepoURL      string         // absolute repository URL
+	Domain       string         // host part of every UID
+	Location     *time.Location // zone the deadlines are pinned in, setting.DefaultUILocation in production
+	Now          time.Time      // DTSTAMP
+}
+
+// ICalUID uses the row ID, never a date or title, so clients move events instead of duplicating them;
+// changing this format duplicates every subscriber's events
+func ICalUID(kind string, id int64, domain string) string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("%s-%d@%s", kind, id, domain)
+}
+
+func newICalendar(opts ICalOptions) *ics.Calendar {
+	cal := ics.NewCalendar()
+	cal.SetProductId("-//Gitea//Gitea " + setting.AppVer + "//EN")
+	cal.SetMethod(ics.MethodPublish)
+	cal.SetCalscale("GREGORIAN")
+	cal.SetXWRCalName(opts.Name)
+	return cal
+}
+
+func addAllDayEvent(cal *ics.Calendar, opts ICalOptions, uid, summary, url string, deadline, updated timeutil.TimeStamp) {
+	day := deadline.AsTimeInLocation(opts.Location) // all-day dates carry no zone, so pick the day where the deadline was set
+	event := cal.AddEvent(uid)
+	event.SetDtStampTime(opts.Now)
+	event.SetModifiedAt(updated.AsTime())
+	event.SetAllDayStartAt(day)
+	event.SetAllDayEndAt(day.AddDate(0, 0, 1)) // DTEND is exclusive
+	event.SetSummary(summary)
+	event.SetURL(url)
+	event.SetDescription(url)
+}
+
+// MilestonesICal lists milestones that have a due date as all-day events
+func MilestonesICal(opts ICalOptions, milestones []*issues_model.Milestone) *ics.Calendar {
+	cal := newICalendar(opts)
+	for _, m := range milestones {
+		if !m.HasDeadline() {
+			continue
+		}
+		addAllDayEvent(cal, opts, ICalUID("milestone", m.ID, opts.Domain),
+			fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", m.Name, opts.RepoFullName),
+			fmt.Sprintf("%s/milestone/%d", opts.RepoURL, m.ID),
+			m.DeadlineUnix, m.UpdatedUnix)
+	}
+	return cal
+}
+
+// IssuesICal lists issues and pull requests that have a deadline as all-day events
+func IssuesICal(opts ICalOptions, issues issues_model.IssueList) *ics.Calendar {
+	cal := newICalendar(opts)
+	for _, issue := range issues {
+		if issue.DeadlineUnix == 0 {
+			continue
+		}
+		path := "issues"
+		if issue.IsPull {
+			path = "pulls"
+		}
+		addAllDayEvent(cal, opts, ICalUID("issue", issue.ID, opts.Domain),
+			fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s#%d)", issue.Title, opts.RepoFullName, issue.Index),
+			fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/%d", opts.RepoURL, path, issue.Index),
+			issue.DeadlineUnix, issue.UpdatedUnix)
+	}
+	return cal
+}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"net/http"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	"gitea.dev/models/unit"
	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
	"gitea.dev/modules/test"
	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
	"gitea.dev/routers/web/feed"
	feed_service "gitea.dev/services/feed"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	ics "github.com/arran4/golang-ical"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestRepoICalFeeds(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	defer timeutil.MockSet(time.Date(2026, 10, 7, 12, 0, 0, 0, setting.DefaultUILocation))()

	deadline := func(date string) timeutil.TimeStamp {
		day, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", date, setting.DefaultUILocation)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		return timeutil.TimeStamp(day.Add(24*time.Hour - time.Second).Unix())
	}
	// public user2/repo1: issue #1 (id 1), pull #2 (id 2), closed issue #4 (id 5); direct DB writes skip the
	// issue indexer, which outlives the test database
	for id, date := range map[int64]string{1: "2026-10-06", 2: "2026-10-30", 5: "2026-10-14"} {
		require.NoError(t, issues_model.UpdateIssueCols(t.Context(), &issues_model.Issue{ID: id, DeadlineUnix: deadline(date)}, "deadline_unix"))
	}
	_, err := db.GetEngine(t.Context()).ID(1).Cols("deadline_unix").Update(&issues_model.Milestone{DeadlineUnix: deadline("2026-10-14")})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	fetch := func(t *testing.T, url string) *ics.Calendar {
		resp := MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", url), http.StatusOK)
		assert.Equal(t, "text/calendar; charset=utf-8", resp.Header().Get("Content-Type"))
		assert.Equal(t, "public, max-age=300", resp.Header().Get("Cache-Control"))
		cal, err := ics.ParseCalendar(resp.Body)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		return cal
	}
	uids := func(cal *ics.Calendar) []string {
		var ids []string
		for _, e := range cal.Events() {
			ids = append(ids, e.Id())
		}
		return ids
	}
	uid := func(kind string, id int64) string { return feed_service.ICalUID(kind, id, setting.Domain) } // the production scheme

	t.Run("milestones with a due date", func(t *testing.T) {
		cal := fetch(t, "/user2/repo1/milestones.ics")
		assert.Equal(t, []string{uid("milestone", 1)}, uids(cal)) // milestone 2 has no date, milestone 3 is closed
		e := cal.Events()[0]
		assert.Equal(t, "milestone1 (user2/repo1)", e.GetProperty(ics.ComponentPropertySummary).Value)
		assert.Equal(t, "20261014", e.GetProperty(ics.ComponentPropertyDtStart).Value)
	})

	t.Run("open issues and pulls by default", func(t *testing.T) {
		cal := fetch(t, "/user2/repo1/issues.ics")
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{uid("issue", 1), uid("issue", 2)}, uids(cal))
	})

	t.Run("state=all adds closed issues", func(t *testing.T) {
		cal := fetch(t, "/user2/repo1/issues.ics?state=all")
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{uid("issue", 1), uid("issue", 2), uid("issue", 5)}, uids(cal))
	})

	t.Run("the cap keeps the closest deadline", func(t *testing.T) {
		defer test.MockVariableValue(&feed.ICalMaxItems, 1)()
		cal := fetch(t, "/user2/repo1/issues.ics")
		assert.Equal(t, []string{uid("issue", 1)}, uids(cal)) // Oct 6 is closer to Oct 7 than Oct 30
	})

	t.Run("a private repo is hidden even from its owner", func(t *testing.T) {
		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		for _, url := range []string{"/user2/repo2/issues.ics", "/user2/repo2/milestones.ics"} {
			MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", url), http.StatusNotFound)
			session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", url), http.StatusNotFound)
		}
	})

	t.Run("disabled feeds", func(t *testing.T) {
		defer test.MockVariableValue(&setting.Other.EnableFeed, false)()
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/issues.ics"), http.StatusNotFound)
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/milestones.ics"), http.StatusNotFound)
	})

	t.Run("subscribe links only where the feed works", func(t *testing.T) {
		for page, link := range map[string]string{
			"/user2/repo1/milestones": "/user2/repo1/milestones.ics",
			"/user2/repo1/issues":     "/user2/repo1/issues.ics",
		} {
			doc := NewHTMLParser(t, MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", page), http.StatusOK).Body)
			assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(`.list-header a[href="`+link+`"]`).Length(), page)
		}
		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		for _, page := range []string{"/user2/repo2/milestones", "/user2/repo2/issues"} {
			doc := NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", page), http.StatusOK).Body)
			assert.Zero(t, doc.Find(`a[href$=".ics"]`).Length(), page) // the private feed would 404
		}
	})

	t.Run("sign-in required hides both feeds", func(t *testing.T) {
		defer test.MockVariableValue(&setting.Service.RequireSignInViewStrict, true)()
		session := loginUser(t, "user2") // a signed-in viewer must not get a public-cacheable feed either
		for _, url := range []string{"/user2/repo1/issues.ics", "/user2/repo1/milestones.ics"} {
			session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", url), http.StatusNotFound)
		}
		for _, page := range []string{"/user2/repo1/issues", "/user2/repo1/milestones"} {
			doc := NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", page), http.StatusOK).Body)
			assert.Zero(t, doc.Find(`a[href$=".ics"]`).Length(), page)
		}
	})

	t.Run("expensive blocking hides only the issues feed", func(t *testing.T) {
		defer test.MockVariableValue(&setting.Service.BlockAnonymousAccessExpensive, true)()
		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/issues.ics"), http.StatusNotFound)
		session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/milestones.ics"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/issues"), http.StatusOK).Body)
		assert.Zero(t, doc.Find(`a[href$="issues.ics"]`).Length())
		doc = NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/milestones"), http.StatusOK).Body)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(`.list-header a[href="/user2/repo1/milestones.ics"]`).Length())
	})

	// must stay last: it deletes repo1's pull request unit
	t.Run("pulls are left out when the pull request unit is off", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, err := db.DeleteByBean(t.Context(), &repo_model.RepoUnit{RepoID: 1, Type: unit.TypePullRequests})
		require.NoError(t, err)
		cal := fetch(t, "/user2/repo1/issues.ics?state=all")
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{uid("issue", 1), uid("issue", 5)}, uids(cal))
	})
}
